For the Petitioner : Mr. Anoop Kumar Mehta, Advocate For the State : Mr. R. Bardhan A.P.P.
 ---------
7/ 31/07/2018 The instant Criminal Revision application has been filed being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the Judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 14.06.2001 passed by 2 nd Additional District and Sessions Judge, Koderma in Cr. Appeal no. 217 of 1990 whereby and whereunder the learned appellate court below has been pleased to affirm the conviction of the petitioner under sections 16-1A(1-2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 passed vide judgment and sentence dated 13.11.1990 by the then S.D.J.M, Koderma in Case No. F.G. 6 of 89 / T.R. No.1424 of 90 whereby and whereunder the petitioner was sentence to undergo Rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years with a fine of Rs. 2,000/- and in default of payment of fine, he was further sentenced to undergo a simple imprisonment for a period of six months.
The case of the prosecution is that one Brij Bhushan Prasad, Food Inspector, Hazaribagh, who was declared as the Food Inspector for the (then) entire district of Hazaribagh vide Ext.9 vide notification of the State Government, inspected the alleged grocery shop of the petitioner Birendra Kumar Barnwal on 24.07.1988 at 2 p.m. situated at Patna-Ranchi road, ward no. 7, Jhumari Telaiya,
Hazaribagh.
The Food Inspector served notice upon the petitioner demanding sample of Haldi powder and mustered oil for sending the same to the Public analyst.

125 X 3 grams of mustered oil and 100 x 3 grams of Haldi powder was purchased by the Food Inspector and by observing all the legal paraphernalia, he sealed three files of mustered oil along with three packets of Haldi powder amounting to 100 grams each and sent the same by registered parcel along with the specimens of Birendra Kumar Barnwal vs The State Of Jharkhand ......... 1 seal and memorandum.

entities.text: Birendra Kumar Barnwal vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further alleged that memorandum and specimen of seal were sent separately to the Public Analyst, Patna, who in course of test found Haldi powder to be adulterated because of the fact that it did not confirm to the prescribed standard and submitted his report accordingly.

The food inspector received the report of the public analyst, Patna and prepared a prosecution report, solicited the sanction from the competent authority and filed the same in the court of the then A.C.J.M., Koderma.
The further case of the prosecution is that one copy of the analyst report was also sent to the petitioner.
This Cr. Revision application was filed on 23.08.2001 and the case was admitted on 17.10.2001 and bail was granted to the petitioner.
Thereafter, on 28.02.2017, L.C.R was called for .

The learned counsel for the petitioner, while assailing the impugned Judgment referred to Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 which reads as under :-
"13. Report of Public Analyst(1).................... (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section(1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated,
the Local(Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any,
whose name address and other particulars have been disclosed under 14-A forward,
in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory".
In view of Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, the mandatory requirement is
that the public analysis report is to be sent to the petitioner, so that he may raise objection and also may apply to the competent court to send the sample for Public Analyst test.
In the instant case, no notice was given to he petitioner, nor copy of the Public Analysis report was also sent to the petitioner.

In para- 8 of the judgment, it has been stated that a copy of the memorandum and seal was separately sent to the Public Analyst vide registered parcel and the rest 2 files of Haldi Powder and mustered oil were sent in the office of the A.C.M.O., Hazaribagh for which a receipt Ext.7 has been produced and marked.
It has further come on evidence that report of the public analyst showing the powder Haldi was received which has been marked Ext.8.
Subsequently, the prosecutions report was filed and accordingly, the prosecution report has been marked Ext.9.

It has also been recorded that the prosecution report along with all the relevant documents were sent to the A.C.M.O.,
Hazaribagh who having been fully satisfied, found the case prima facie true and accorded sanction and sanctioned order was marked Ext. 10 and copy of the public analyst report was sent to the petitioner through a registered post for which a postal receipt has been produced which was marked Ext.11.

sentences.text:
It is further clear from the record that public analyst report was sent to the petitioner through registered post and name and address which was written under section 313 Cr.P.C has been violated,
he has not received the notice and may apply before the competent court to send the sample to the public analyst.
This fact has not been taken into consideration by the courts below.
The learned A.P.P referred to Ext. 11 and submitted that notice was sent to the petitioner.
The prosecution had given his address in Ext- 11 in a cryptic manner and so, the petitioner could not receive the notice and so, there is no violation of the provision under section 313 of Cr.P.C
Both courts have correctly taken into consideration this fact while passing the order and judgments.

In view of the facts that the prosecution has failed to comply with mandatory provision provided under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, both the Judgments and orders passed by the courts below are hereby set aside.
Accordingly, this Criminal Revision is allowed.
The petitioner is discharged from the liabilities of his bail bonds.
Let the Lower Court Record be sent to the court concerned forthwith.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the trial court through FAX.
On 28.2.2017 a Coordinate Bench of this Court had called for the LCR and had directed to list this case immediately after receipt of the Lower court Records.

Perused the office note dated 17.4.2018, which reveals that letter bearing No. 248/17 dated 11.4.2017, kept at Flag"A" submitted by Divya Mishra S.D.J.M Koderma has not been placed before this court or any Bench and it has been listed today for the first time.

Letter reveals that LCR of F.G Case No. 6 of 1989 T.R. No. 1424 of 1990 was transmitted to the court of Sri. Ekramuddin, the then Judicial Magistrate, Koderma on 18.1.1989 and the trial register of that court for the year 1989 is traceless, so the LCR cannot be located.

sentences.text: It further appears that another two reminders were sent to the court concerned on 21.122017 and on 23.3.2018 and only on 13.4.2018 learned S.D.J.M Koderma has informed that the records of F.G Case No. 6 of 1989 T.R. No. 1424 of 1990 is still missing and Principal District Judge, Koderma has held an inquiry in the matter Vide order dated 08.05.2018, Registrar (Vigilance) was directed to hold inquiry and, if required, to visit the District Court, Koderma after obtaining necessary permission from Hon'ble the Acting Chief Justice and to submit a report this court.

Pursuant thereto, the Registrar (Vigilance) has submitted his report dated 25.06.2018 which reads as under :-
"Prior to visit of the Judgeship, undersigned perused the case record of Cr.Rev No.
339 of 2001 on 25.6.2018.On perusal of the record

it transpires that in the meantime the original case record of F.G Case No. 06 of 1989,T.R No. 1424 of 1990 has been received in the section on 22.5.2018 with letter no. 293 of 2018 dated 21.5.2018 of Birendra Kumar Barnwal vs The State Of Jharkhand .........

Said Officer has intimated that earlier due to wrong reporting of the Officer-in-charge of District Record Room of Koderma it was intimidated that original case record was traceless, however on intensive search after initiation of inquiry by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Koderma with the help of the Staff of Civil court, the original case record has been traced out from the District Record Room, Koderma and it has been sent accordingly.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, he has reported that one paper i.e. ext 6 is missing from the said record.
Therefore, presently the original record has already been received in the Hon'ble Court."
Let the report of Registrar (Vigilance) along this Judgment be placed before the Zonal Judge with request to pass appropriate order.
